scope: Unpublished local Roblox Studio review of Normal M1-M6 in sequence on the immutable production place artifact. This is not published Roblox Player acceptance and does not evaluate remote PR #84.

verdict.summary: LOCAL M1-M4 PLAYABLE; M5 SEQUENTIAL BLOCKER REPRODUCED; M6 LOCKED/UNOBSERVED; REJECT M1-M6 BLOCK ACCEPTANCE
verdict.reason: M1-M4 completed through authoritative outcomes. Four legitimate M5 attempts failed before the 2,000-point phase could finish; the best reached 1,270 points and 21 targets at 8:14 before a terrain collision. M6 remained locked because no M5 win was fabricated.

studioLease.closure: Studio MCP stopped Play. TERM did not exit; KILL was sent only to owned PID 51909. Studio list then returned empty. StudioMCP/helper processes were not killed.

manualNative: Mouse-operated flight-record, aircraft-change, sticky launch, cinematic skip, continue, pause, resume and retry buttons.
Keyboard E throttle, W pitch, Tab target cycle, Space missile and held G gun were directly operated in M1; native launch/continue/retry controls were used throughout.
Pause overlay was opened by its actual button because the injected P key was processed without toggling in that moment.
inputDisclosure.productionControllerAutomation: After manual input checks, temporary client-context LocalScripts obtained FlightController.GetActive() and used only public SetInput, SetThrottle, CycleTarget, FireMissile, FireGun, Evade, Rearm, SetPaused and read-only telemetry/state methods. Automation never set position/CFrame, health, score, kills, ammo, unlocks, clocks, outcomes or progress.
inputDisclosure.automationPurpose: Sustained legitimate combat coverage and navigation; not evidence of human flight feel.
inputDisclosure.clockIntegrity: No clock acceleration. Pauses were limited to the presentation check and automation handoffs. M5 attempts ran their real elapsed clocks until their authoritative failures.
inputDisclosure.diagnostics: Temporary QA56 LocalScripts printed telemetry and were removed before Play stopped. Direct tool-context module calls that returned an unrelated context were not used as gameplay evidence.

missions.name: Sitting Duck
observations: Fresh local record began at M1. Both F-4E and F-5E were selectable; Change updated the sticky launch button to F-5E.
The six required Tu-95s produced the authoritative 600-point result. Manual control/weapon inputs preceded production-controller coverage.
The flight showed a compact objective card, telemetry, radar, target boxes and a long two-line radio caption without caption/objective overlap at the 1205x525 client viewport.
missions.referenceComparison: The six 100-point Tu-95 requirement and broadly linear forward interception agree with the Mitoro M01 table/route. The local islands, aircraft and structures remain sparse blocks rather than an AC04-specific representation.

missions.name: Imminent Threat
observations: All eleven parked Tu-95 required targets were destroyed through real hits for the source-matched 1,320 score.
The automation finished at 22 hull, demonstrating substantial incoming damage rather than a protected scripted pass.
The airfield encounter was readable as a runway/apron concentration, but the runway aircraft launch behavior and richer base staging described by the reference were not confirmed.
missions.referenceComparison: Mitoro M02 lists eleven Tu-95s at 120 points and a dense Rigley airfield pass using both missiles and gun. Count/score matched; runway-takeoff staging remained unverified.

missions.name: The Northern Eye
observations: All nine radar targets were destroyed, then the live objective changed to Return south to allied territory.

The HUD showed PHASE ELAPSED, RETURN LINE · SOUTH (180°), a live south-to-line distance, north-to-south crossing wording and no altitude limit. Completion occurred only after crossing the actual southern line.
Pause hid SkybreakFlightTargeting (DisplayOrder 5) under the campaign overlay (DisplayOrder 10); Resume restored it.
missions.referenceComparison: The two ground clusters followed by a simple southbound second phase agrees structurally with Mitoro M03. The implemented guidance is clearer than the old review, but geography remained abstract and exact map-scale fidelity was not rated.

missions.name: Blockade
observations: The three moving C-17 transports were intercepted for 160 points each. A stable close-range gun/reattack approach was required after an initial directly-behind orbit produced no progress.
The result text correctly connected cutting the transport route to isolating Comberth's reserves.
Two E-767/jamming presentation and the source-specific reinforcement patterns after each C-17 were not conclusively observed during the required-target run.
missions.referenceComparison: Required C-17 count/points match Mitoro M04. The source describes north-east movement, two distinct E-767 jamming regions and reinforcement patterns after transports; only the required moving transport corridor was verified here.

missions.name: Lifeline
observations: The real ten-minute 2,000-point phase started and accepted legitimate air/ground/naval hits. No score, target or timer was injected.

Southern-line Rearm was exercised successfully during attempt 3: the live Base control serviced/weapons replenished radio appeared and hull/ammo returned to 100/48/650. This was real server-authoritative service, not state mutation.
Plain-language enemy-fire and terrain-collision debriefs both appeared live.
The best attempt survived 8:14, killed 21 targets and reached only 1,270 before terrain collision. No withdrawal/offshore phase or Yellow Squadron encounter was reached.

Current source places the full baseline F-16 7 + MiG-29 13 + MIR-2000 7 + Ka-50 3 roster into phase 0 without afterGroup/triggerAt staging; AC04World initially exposes every phase-0 untriggered group. The Mitoro M05 guide instead describes aircraft appearing later, including MiG-29s after enough refinery destruction. This is a concrete pacing/fidelity mismatch and a credible contributor to immediate threat density.

Because the blocker occurred under controller automation rather than a skilled human pilot, this evidence proves failure of these four legitimate attempts and the staging mismatch, not that every human player is mathematically unable to win.

missions.name: Invincible Fleet
missions.reason: Sequential campaign progression correctly kept M6 locked after M5 did not complete. No unlock or outcome was spoofed.
missions.referenceComparison: Mitoro M06 distinguishes the fleet, Comberth harbor, New Comberth harbor and shipyard; Tanager has four components and fighter respawns depend on local clearance. None of this received live verification. Known Normal manifest uncertainty remains open.

story.assessment: The two named chapters preserved the intended civilian-war framing in original wording, but their visible scenes were primitive block tableaus with minimal authored detail. This does not yet look or feel specifically like AC04's restrained illustrated interludes.

ac04PresentationCriterion.assessment: The start flow clearly labels ACE COMBAT 04 · SHATTERED SKIES and uses a coherent restrained dark/teal campaign UI, but it reads as a functional SKYBREAK menu themed with AC04 text rather than an AC04-specific strategic briefing/deployment presentation.
prioritizedRecommendations: P1: Replace the briefing's text-only expanse with mission-specific strategic map geometry, objective/route markers and aircraft/loadout framing derived from the AC04 reference structure while retaining original art/text.
P1: Replace the most visible primitive interlude/tableau silhouettes and uniform block aircraft with deliberate original illustrated story panels and recognizable mission aircraft silhouettes.
P1: Stage M5 aircraft in source-backed waves/conditions instead of presenting the complete baseline fighter roster at phase start; then retest score pacing, survival and withdrawal.
P2: Add concrete M4 E-767 jamming-region feedback and source-shaped transport/reinforcement routes; verify them live rather than describing generic airborne jamming.

findings.title: M5 blocks sequential M1-M6 local acceptance
findings.evidence: Four authoritative failures: 0/240/1270/210 scores at 1:22/1:50/8:14/2:00. M6 remained locked.
findings.recommendation: Reconcile M5 wave/respawn staging to source, calibrate Normal threat/score pacing, then independently replay M5 through the timer, withdrawal and offshore phase before attempting M6.

findings.title: M5 baseline fighter groups are simultaneous where the reference describes later appearances
findings.evidence: AC04MissionData M5 gives F-16 7, MiG-29 13, MIR-2000 7 and Ka-50 3 no triggers; AC04World initially exposes phase-0 untriggered groups. Mitoro M05 describes later mass arrivals and refinery-destruction-triggered MiG-29s.
findings.recommendation: Author source-backed trigger/respawn conditions and record Normal-specific uncertainty rather than collapsing the minimum roster into one initial threat cloud.

findings.title: Start/briefing/story art is coherent but not yet specifically AC04 in look and feel
findings.evidence: Text-led start/briefing, sparse block aircraft/worlds and primitive story tableaus; no mission strategic-map/deployment visual was observed.
findings.recommendation: Prioritize mission-specific strategic briefing visuals and authored story/aircraft silhouettes over generic polish.

findings.title: M4 required result is correct but jammer/reinforcement fidelity remains unproven
findings.evidence: Three C-17s produced 480, but the two E-767 jamming regions and transport-kill reinforcement patterns were not conclusively observed.
findings.recommendation: Instrument and replay M4 while deliberately entering each E-767 region and observing every C-17-triggered reinforcement.
